scenarios.name: C-Bet: Dry High Board
scenarios.description: GTO continuation bet strategy on dry high boards (e.g. K-7-2 rainbow)

scenarios.name: C-Bet: Wet Connected Board
scenarios.description: GTO continuation bet strategy on wet connected boards (e.g. J-T-9 two-tone)

scenarios.name: C-Bet: Paired Board
scenarios.description: GTO continuation bet strategy on paired boards (e.g. 8-8-3 rainbow)

scenarios.name: C-Bet: Monotone Board
scenarios.description: GTO continuation bet strategy on monotone boards (e.g. 9-7-3 all spades)

scenarios.name: Turn: Brick Card
scenarios.description: GTO turn strategy when the turn is a low, non-threatening card that does not change the board texture significantly (e.g. 3c on a K-7-2r flop)

scenarios.name: Turn: Flush-Completing Card
scenarios.description: GTO turn strategy when the turn completes a possible flush draw on the flop (e.g. fourth heart on a three-heart flop)

scenarios.name: Turn: Straight-Completing Card
scenarios.description: GTO turn strategy when the turn card completes a possible straight draw (e.g. 8 on a K-7-6 flop creates 7-8 straight draws)

scenarios.name: Turn: Overcard to Flop Top Pair
scenarios.description: GTO turn strategy when the turn brings an overcard to the flop's top pair (e.g. Ace on a King-high flop), shifting hand strengths significantly

scenarios.name: River: Blank Card
scenarios.description: GTO river strategy when the river is a blank that does not complete any draws or significantly alter the board (e.g. 4d on a K-7-2-3c board)

scenarios.name: River: Scary Card (Flush or Straight Completes)
scenarios.description: GTO river strategy when the river completes a flush or straight draw, requiring adjusted ranges for both value bets and bluffs

scenarios.name: River: Paired Board
scenarios.description: GTO river strategy when the river pairs the board, introducing the possibility of full houses and shifting optimal bet sizes
